classification.difficultyReason: Complete four squares, including negative leading coefficients, derive exact surd intercepts and recognise quadratics with no real zeroes before sketching.

content.prompt: Complete the square for each quadratic. Then sketch the graph of each function, showing the vertex and the intercepts with the axes.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(x^2+2x+1)-1-5\\y&=(x+1)^2-6\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-1,-6)$ and the parabola opens upwards. At $x=0$, $y=-5$.
For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2-6&=0\\(x+1)^2&=6\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt6\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt6\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled vertex and all axis intercepts; no grid.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-y&=x^2-6x+6\\-y&=(x^2-6x+9)-9+6\\-y&=(x-3)^2-3\\y&=-(x-3)^2+3\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(3,3)$ and the parabola opens downwards. At $x=0$, $y=-6$.
For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-(x-3)^2+3&=0\\(x-3)^2&=3\\x-3&=\pm\sqrt3\\x&=3\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Downward parabola with labelled vertex and all axis intercepts; no grid.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-y&=x^2-2x+3\\-y&=(x^2-2x+1)-1+3\\-y&=(x-1)^2+2\\y&=-(x-1)^2-2\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(1,-2)$ and the parabola opens downwards. Since $-(x-1)^2-2\leq-2$, there are no $x$-intercepts. At $x=0$, $y=-3$. By symmetry, $(2,-3)$ is also on the graph.

spec.description: Downward parabola wholly below the x-axis, with vertex, y-intercept, symmetric point and dashed symmetry guides.

$$\begin{align*}y&=(x^2+6x+9)-9+10\\y&=(x+3)^2+1\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-3,1)$ and the parabola opens upwards. Since $(x+3)^2+1\geq1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. At $x=0$, $y=10$. By symmetry, $(-6,10)$ is also on the graph.
